relevance_note: The paper reports two children with HA20: "We also diagnosed two cases of haploinsufficiency of A20 (HA20)" and names their TNFAIP3 variants ("p.R271X of the TNFAIP3 gene in one patient and p.R45X in the other one").
method_note: Read the paper, schema and rules by hand; no script transcribed any table. In scope are only the two HA20 patients of this single-centre AID cohort; the other 77 diagnosed patients (Blau, TRAPS, DADA2, PAID, Majeed, AGS, SAVI, SPENCD, PRAAS, NLRP3/NLRP12/PLCG2/NLRC4/MEFV/MVK cases) get no rows and are covered by cohort_size_as_stated. The paper labels the two HA20 patients only as "one patient"/"the other one" (role words), so they were given 'unnamed person 1' and 'unnamed person 2' in order of first mention; 'unnamed person 1' is the patient said to have been "diagnosed as Behçet disease previously". The variant sentence "The genetic sequencing yielded p.R271X of the TNFAIP3 gene in one patient and p.R45X in the other one" does not say which patient carries which variant, and Table 2 is a disease-level table (one row per disease, variants p.R45X, p.R271X in one cell, no patient rows, no per-patient reference column); so no variant could be assigned to a named individual: both patients keep a variant row with variant_original_string 'not reported' and no per-person variant fields (D-29). Table 2's "Inheritance: AD" column belongs to the disease row, not to a person, so inheritance is 'not reported' for both. The disease-level Table 2 row for A20 deficiency ("Fever, rash, arthralgia, mucosal ulcers, bowel inflammation, CTD") lists features for the pair as a group, not for a named person, so no phenotypic_features rows were derived from it. Group statements used: "both suffered from recurrent oral ulcer" (the two HA20 patients, the group the paper is discussing) -> oral ulcers observed for both, evidence_basis 'inferred from group statement'; "Hashimoto′s thyroiditis was also found in one patient" names no person and is a 1-of-2 count, so it excludes/assigns nothing; "There was no consanguinity in these children" is a group statement about the study children, and the two HA20 patients are the only in-scope members of that group, so individuals.consanguinity is 'no' for both (no phenotypic_features row: consanguinity is not a clinical feature); "For Blau syndrome, DADA2 and HA20 patients, we initiated anti-TNF-α therapies and have observed some good responses" names the HA20 group and is recorded as both patients' treatment_summary. The paper states no sex, age, ethnicity, vital status or per-patient treatment for either HA20 patient, and does not report parental testing. No contradictions were found in the paper. No stacked (' / ') cell involves an in-scope patient: the only stacked cell with ' / ' is the ADA2 deficiency variant cell of Table 2, which is out of scope.

first_author.span: Authors: Wang Wei; Yu Zhongxun; Gou Lijuan; Zhong Linqing; Li Ji; Ma Mingsheng; Wang Changyan; Zhou Yu; Ru Ying; Sun Zhixing; Wei Qijiao; Dong Yanqing; Song Hongmei

study_type.span: Single-Center Overview of Pediatric Monogenic Autoinflammatory Diseases in the Past Decade: A Summary and Beyond

cohort_size_as_stated.span: A total of 288 pediatric patients (age 18 or less) suspected of having monogenic AIDs were included in this study at the Peking Union Medical Hospital between November 2008 and May 2019.

individual_label_in_paper.span: For our patients, both suffered from recurrent oral ulcer. One patient was diagnosed as Behçet disease previously and the other one was diagnosed with undifferentiated connective tissue disease.

ethnicity_or_country.span: This is by far the first and largest monogenic AID report in Chinese pediatric population

consanguinity.span: There was no consanguinity in these children.

treatment_summary.span: For Blau syndrome, DADA2 and HA20 patients, we initiated anti-TNF-α therapies and have observed some good responses.

disease_label_as_stated.span: We also diagnosed two cases of haploinsufficiency of A20 (HA20).

clinical_diagnosis_basis.value: genetic sequencing of TNFAIP3 with clinical phenotypes (genotype-phenotype verification)
span: Final definite diagnoses were made when the phenotypes and genotypes were mutually verified.
The genetic sequencing yielded p.R271X of the TNFAIP3 gene in one patient and p.R45X in the other one, which were known to be pathogenic variants (25, 26).
